levelMapping: SE2 (Software Engineer 2) ≈ Google L4, typically 2–5 YOE; Senior Software Engineer (SSE) ≈ L5, 5+ YOE. A strong 3.3-YOE candidate lands SE2 in Bengaluru (SE2 offers reported at ~₹27–30L base / ~₹40–45L total). Intuit is known to down-level aggressively vs FAANG titles — confirm the level with the recruiter, and note strong SE2 performance occasionally gets upgraded to SSE.

process.summary: Intuit runs its 'Assessing for Awesome' (A4A) loop: OA (Glider in India, HackerRank for early-career) → 1–2 technical phone screens (TPI: DSA + design + AI discussion) → a craft assignment → a same-day virtual onsite of 4 back-to-back rounds: Craft Demonstration (the signature, make-or-break round, 60–90 min with ~4 panelists), Assessor/technical (DSA + craft follow-ups), a dedicated AI round (added ~early 2025), and Hiring Manager. The craft is either (a) a pre-shared GitHub repo (github.com/Intuit-A4A 'player service' — Java Spring Boot/H2 or Python Flask/SQLite, integrated with a local Ollama tinyllama LLM) in which you implement user stories live, or (b) an open-ended take-home (bidding system, marketplace, leaderboard, etc.) built over 2 days–1 week and then demoed and defended. Production-quality code, unit tests, error handling and correct HTTP semantics are scored hard — candidates have been rejected purely on error codes and exception handling.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, role/level fit, comp expectations, loop logistics; increasingly asks how you use AI tools day-to-day.
rounds.probes: Which craft variant you'll get (repo vs take-home vs live build) — ask explicitly; level being targeted.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.what: Glider.ai in India (sometimes HackerRank/HackerEarth): typically 1–2 DSA problems (easy–medium: linked-list palindrome, merge sorted lists, greedy/grid problems) + ~5 MCQs on Java, OOP, design patterns, SQL, REST. 2026 SE1 flow via the 'Uptime Crew' vendor: 1 DSA + 1 SQL + 1 Bash in 90 min, proctored.
rounds.probes: Speed and correctness; MCQs are timed (~1 min each).

rounds.name: TPI technical phone screen
rounds.what: Intro + project deep-dive, then 1–3 LC-medium DSA problems coded and run live; plus HLD mini-discussion (CAP, scaling a DB, capacity) and since 2025 an AI segment (RAG, LLM basics, how you use GenAI). Staff screens are formally split 35–45 min LeetCode + 30–35 min AI Q&A.
rounds.probes: Edge cases, complexity, running the code against interviewer test cases; resume/system deep-dives ('how did you handle 100M events').

rounds.name: Craft preparation (take-home)
rounds.duration: 2 days–1 week (or 90 min live for some US loops)
rounds.what: Either set up the pre-shared Intuit-A4A repo locally (Java Spring Boot + H2 + Ollama, or Python Flask + SQLite + Ollama) and prepare an intro PPT, or build an open-ended app (bidding system, marketplace, leaderboard...) with APIs, DB, unit/integration tests, HLD/LLD diagrams and a short deck.
rounds.probes: Working demo, test coverage, API contracts, DB schema, design patterns, assumptions documented.

rounds.name: Craft Demonstration
rounds.what: PPT self-intro + proudest project, then demo. Repo variant: implement 1–2 user stories live (add a POST/GET API with service layer, isAdmin filtering, call the LLM endpoint, pagination), run it in Postman, write JUnit/pytest tests. Take-home variant: walk through your app and defend it.
rounds.probes: Error/exception handling and HTTP status codes (a known rejection reason), edge cases, PUT vs PATCH, path vs query params, DB design, pagination, security/rate limiting, scaling the same design; AI coding assistants must be disabled (candidates asked to turn off Copilot).

rounds.name: Assessor / technical round
rounds.what: 1–2 LC-medium DSA problems (often on Glider, any language) + follow-ups extending the craft (add pagination/sorting, schema changes, API versioning), SQL queries, Java/Spring internals, concurrency.
rounds.probes: Brute force → optimal with complexity; production-ready code; monolith vs microservices, scaling, caching, thundering herd, exponential backoff.

rounds.name: Team member round
rounds.what: Cross-functional colleague; lighter discussion of craft HLD/LLD, current project, design patterns, caching, sometimes a small design prompt; Intuit-values flavoured questions.
rounds.probes: Pros/cons and improvements of your own craft design; debugging a production issue.

rounds.name: AI round
rounds.what: Dedicated AI assessment added ~early 2025 for all SWE loops: what is RAG, system prompts, LLM temperature, embeddings/vector DBs, agentic AI vs GenAI, when to use (and not use) AI; sometimes hands-on — write a prompt that forces strict JSON output, or sketch an LLM-calling user story; occasionally classic-ML trivia (k-means, model training).
rounds.probes: Practical judgment ('when should AI NOT be used'), unit testing/monitoring for the craft APIs, hallucination handling in a financial product.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.what: Behavioral + light technical: project deep-dive, caching/latency/peak-load talk, why Intuit, work pressure, team fit; mapped loosely to Intuit values (Integrity Without Compromise, Courage, Customer Obsession, Stronger Together, We Care and Give Back).
rounds.probes: Ownership and customer-impact stories; occasionally estimation ('will 1B student objects fit in memory', 'design a page-visit counter').

process.indiaNotes: Bengaluru runs the full A4A loop, almost always virtual, with the 4 onsite rounds back-to-back on one day (breaks in between; HM round often rescheduled). OA is on Glider.ai for SE2/SSE; 2025-26 SE1/new-grad hiring is outsourced to 'Uptime Crew' (OA → recruiter 1:1 → multi-hour 'Build Challenge' → tech screen on the challenge → craft/A4A). Backend loops are strongly Java/Spring Boot flavoured (craft repo options are Java or Python only); frontend loops use React + a UI craft (event manager, weather app, sports registration). SE2 hires at 2–5 YOE (several accepted offers at 1.9–3 YOE). Reported SE2 comp: ₹27L base + ₹7.25L/yr stock + ₹3L bonus (Aug 2025), ₹42.3L TC (Jan 2025). Recruiters are widely reported as slow/unresponsive between stages; weekend hiring drives happen (e.g. Jan 2025 drive).
process.timeline: 2–6 weeks typical: OA within days of recruiter contact, phone screen ~1 week later, craft assigned with 2 days–2 weeks of prep, onsite loop on one day, verdict in 1 day–2 weeks. Delays of 3–4 months due to panel availability have been reported.
tips: The craft is the loop — later rounds (assessor, team member, HM) all keep probing it. Prepare an HLD diagram (Excalidraw/Draw.io), a short PPT, and know the 'why' of every line and dependency.

If given the Intuit-A4A player-service repo, practice beforehand: clone it (github.com/Intuit-A4A/backend-java-player-service or backend-python-player-service), run it with Ollama/tinyllama, and rehearse adding a paginated GET, a POST with validation, and an endpoint that calls the LLM — with tests.
Error handling decides offers: proper HTTP status codes, global exception handling, validation and negative-path unit tests were explicitly cited in a rejection.
Write tests without being asked — JUnit/integration tests carry real weight in craft scoring; 'no tests' is a stated red flag.
Keep the take-home simple but complete: SOLID, a design pattern or two you can justify, clean DB schema, Postman collection; finishing beats fancy architecture.

Prepare the AI round seriously even for pure backend roles: RAG, embeddings, vector DBs, temperature, prompt-to-strict-JSON exercises, and 2–3 concrete stories of using AI at work; several otherwise-strong candidates were dinged here.

Java fluency matters in Bengaluru: rounds have required coding in Java specifically (threading, Runnable/Callable, singleton, producer-consumer with BlockingQueue, HashMap internals, Spring bean lifecycle).

DSA is LC-medium, favourite areas: linked lists, trees (delete-node-to-forest), grids/BFS, DP (edit distance, house robber), heaps/top-K, median of stream. Explain brute force first, then optimize, then run the code.
Expect disabled AI assistants during the live craft; some interviewers allow plain internet for syntax, many don't — ask.
Confirm your craft variant and level with the recruiter up front; the process shifts between SE2/SSE mid-loop and down-leveling is common.
process.notes: OA platform: Glider.ai (India SE2+), HackerRank/HackerEarth (early career), 'Uptime Crew' vendor pipeline for 2025-26 SE1 (OA with DSA+SQL+Bash, then a 2–5 hour Build Challenge: two problem statements in Java/Python with OOP, design patterns, DB persistence, unit tests and a README, submitted as a private repo). The loop name is 'Assessing for Awesome' (A4A). A dedicated AI interview was added to every SWE loop around Q1 2025. Values round folds into team-member/HM rounds (Intuit values: Integrity Without Compromise, Courage, Customer Obsession, Stronger Together, We Care and Give Back). The craft-demo repo is public: github.com/Intuit-A4A (player-service, Java Spring Boot 3/H2/Ollama4j or Python Flask/SQLite/Ollama tinyllama). Candidate sentiment on Glassdoor/Blind flags unresponsive recruiters and occasional hostile/opinionated panels, especially on system design rounds.

lld.title: A4A player-service repo: implement user stories live (THE craft demo)
lld.prompt: Pre-shared repo (github.com/Intuit-A4A — Java Spring Boot 3/JPA/H2 or Python Flask/SQLite, integrated with Ollama running tinyllama in Docker) serving baseball player data. Live, you pick/get user stories such as: add a GET/POST players API with validation and error handling; filter response fields by an isAdmin query param (admins see first+last names, regular users only first names); add an endpoint that takes a prompt, calls the local LLM API, and returns its response (e.g. generate a player nickname by country); add pagination and sorting to the list API; write JUnit/pytest tests for everything.
lld.deliverable: Working code run live (Postman demo) + unit tests, with AI assistants disabled; repo shared 24h–1 week ahead for local setup
probes: error/exception handling and HTTP status codes (cited rejection reason)
REST conventions (PUT vs PATCH, path vs query params)
pagination internals (JPA Specification, limit/offset edge cases)
then scaled up in the next round (caching, rate limiting, many instances)
lld.evidence: Dominant 2024–2026 format: Dec 2024, May 2025, Jun 2025, Jul 2025, Aug 2025, Oct 2025 reports all describe this repo

lld.title: Bidding system backend (take-home craft)
lld.prompt: Build the backend for an auction platform: vendors put products up for bidding in a date/time slot; registered users browse by category and bid; bids below base price must error; at slot end, pick the winner and send a communication. Aim for microservices with well-defined API contracts (REST/GraphQL), correct status codes and error handling, a clean data model with justified DB choice, TDD/good unit-test coverage, and design patterns where applicable; bonus for a production NFR strategy.
lld.deliverable: Working app + HLD/LLD diagrams + PPT, built over ~2 days–1 week, demoed to a 4-person panel
lld.evidence: Verbatim SWE-2 backend craft statement shared Oct 2024; bidding design also in Nov 2024 phone screen

lld.title: Freelance marketplace (Upwork-style jobs + bids)
lld.prompt: Build a marketplace: sellers post projects with requirements and a bid deadline; buyers (self-employed) bid fixed-price or hourly; lowest bid auto-wins at deadline and is displayed on the project page; homepage shows the 100 most recent projects. Scale hints: 50K buyers, 100 projects/day, ~50 bids/project. Frontend candidates may mock the backend; full-stack builds both (in-memory DB acceptable).
lld.deliverable: Working prototype demoed live (one US candidate built it in the 90-min on-the-day variant; India usually gets days)
probes: implement 'create job' or 'top 10 jobs' API live
lld.evidence: Glassdoor craft statement; Senior SWE onsite Nov 2023 built the same prompt

lld.title: Top-K game leaderboard module
lld.prompt: Given an online game service, build a module that returns the top K scorers (name + score), handling streaming score updates. Shared 2 days ahead as a machine-coding take-home with full LLD expected.
lld.deliverable: LLD + working code + optional presentation to the panel
lld.evidence: SDE2 Jun 2022 craft; 'gaming module leaderboard top-K' craft again May 2024

lld.title: Transaction reconciliation engine (Buyer.csv vs Supplier.csv)
lld.prompt: Given two CSVs of transactions (buyer-side and supplier-side), build a service that matches them into Exact / Partial / Only-in-Buyer / Only-in-Supplier categories. Partial matching: numbers within ±threshold, dates within ±threshold, fuzzy string similarity; surface the best partial match when several exist.
lld.deliverable: Working code + design, given ~5 days ahead; one candidate's solution is public on GitHub (TransactionMatchingService)
lld.evidence: SDE2 Jul 2022 (full statement); 'transaction similarity scoring' craft again Jun 2022; QuickBooks-reconciliation theme recurs

lld.title: Car-pooling application (BlaBlaCar-style)
lld.prompt: Build a running car-pooling app: drivers post rides, riders search and book seats. Candidate negotiated 4 days and built it in Spring Boot; panel of 4 ran their own test cases against the live app.
lld.deliverable: Running application demoed against panel-supplied test cases

lld.title: Microservice over a CSV with rate-limited APIs + Docker
lld.prompt: Create a microservice that reads records from a data source (CSV standing in for a DB) and exposes get-all and get-by-id APIs plus a rate-limiting API; include scripts to package it as a Docker image. Language free (one candidate chose Go).
lld.deliverable: Take-home assignment, then design+code+demo presentation in round 1
probes: how to paginate the APIs / SQL paging
rate limiting across multiple instances (queue-based and LB-based designs)
algorithms used by distributed in-memory DBs
lld.evidence: SDE2 platform loop Nov 2023; 'backend API over a CSV dataset' again in SSE Bengaluru loop Dec 2025

lld.title: Rate limiter (working code)
lld.prompt: Implement a working rate limiter using fixed-window or sliding-window; discussion established a queue-backed implementation over a plain map.
lld.evidence: SSE loop Feb 2024; rate limiting recurs as a craft follow-up in many loops

lld.title: Multi-level comment service
lld.prompt: Build a working comment service for a social product supporting replies-on-replies (arbitrary nesting), with ORM-backed persistence.
lld.deliverable: Fully working code demoed in the craft round

lld.title: Driver onboarding module for a ride platform
lld.prompt: Build the driver-onboarding slice of a ride-management platform: registration, document collection, verification states, activation.
lld.deliverable: Candidate shipped a PPT, flow/sequence diagrams, integration tests, 11 working APIs and an optional React frontend over ~3 days; presented in two separate onsite rounds
probes: pros/cons and improvements of your own design
production-ready extension coded live in the acceptor round
lld.round: Craft assessment + Craft demo + Team member round

lld.title: Build Challenge (2026 SE1/SE2 Uptime Crew pipeline)
lld.prompt: Two problem statements completed in a timed live/take-home setup (2–5 hours) in Java or Python: object-oriented design (classes, inheritance, encapsulation), design patterns where justified, database persistence, integration of provided 'Insight Services', unit tests for major cases, and a clear README, submitted as a private repo.
lld.deliverable: Private repo link before the deadline; a later 30-min tech screen dissects it (approach, alternatives, data modeling, constraints)
probes: defend every line several layers deep
lld.evidence: SDE-1 selected report Apr 2026; Build Challenge threads Jan–Mar 2026

lld.title: Event management system (frontend craft)
lld.prompt: Build an event management app (create/list/manage events) as the frontend craft; ~1 week prep, then demo with PPT, code walkthrough and live modifications (e.g. sort the rendered list on the spot).
lld.deliverable: Working UI + tests + PPT; meaningful (condition-asserting) test cases expected, not just coverage
probes: test quality ('what's the use of a test that checks no condition?')

lld.title: Weather app (UI craft)
lld.prompt: Build a weather application with several specified features as the UI craft assessment.

lld.title: Sports event registration UI (frontend craft)
lld.prompt: Build a UI for sports-event registration; candidate added a Confluence design doc, unit tests with 100% coverage (lcov report) and an improvement roadmap — and got the offer.

lld.title: Book exchange system (craft)
lld.prompt: Design and build a book exchange system (users list books, request swaps). Panel reportedly values clean API design, exception handling, response codes, API security (Basic/OAuth), containerization and load balancing between containers.
lld.deliverable: Working app + diagrams ('fancy diagrams' explicitly rewarded); sample candidate codebases exist on GitHub
lld.evidence: Craft thread Mar 2023 with Intuit-interviewer-adjacent replies; 3-day SSE variant with NFRs (rate limiting, retry, gateway, OAuth) Sep 2024

lld.title: In-session mini-LLD: stack/queue builds and OOD classics
lld.prompt: Shorter LLD asks inside assessor rounds: implement a stack using queues; implement Singleton and Factory patterns in code; a Decorator-pattern exercise; make a Java class immutable; design a parking lot (reported via aggregator).
lld.deliverable: Compiling code or whiteboard class design within the round
lld.evidence: Stack-using-queues Oct 2024; Singleton/Factory Aug 2022; Decorator Mar 2025; immutability Aug 2023

lld.title: Prompt-engineering exercise: strict JSON output (AI round)
lld.prompt: Using ChatGPT live, write a prompt that makes the model return only a correct JSON object (shaped like an API response body) for any given input, covering edge cases — a hands-on task in the eliminator/AI round.
probes: why/when to use an LLM at all
lld.evidence: SDE2 eliminator round Jun 2025; 'use ChatGPT to solve a problem' also in Senior loop Sep 2025
